t: None of the funds made available to NASA in this Act may be used for voluntary separation incentive payments as provided for in subchapter II of chapter 35 of title 5, United States Code, unless the Administrator of NASA has first certified to Congress that such payments would not result in the loss of skills related to the safety of the Space Shuttle or the International Space Station or to the conduct of independent safety oversight in the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the required certification as a procedural check before a federal decision. That certification runs from the NASA Administrator to Congress, and both are inside the federal government. No state, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing, or granted a right to sue, so this appropriations restriction is not participation.
fable.s: unless the Administrator of NASA has first certified to Congress that such payments would not result in the loss of skills

opus.w: Before using funds for separation incentive payments, the NASA Administrator must certify to Congress, which is inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and the section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. A formal pre-decision step looks procedural, but it never crosses the federal boundary, so this is not participation.
opus.s: unless the Administrator of NASA has first certified to Congress that such payments would not result in the loss of skills related to the safety of the Space Shuttle
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the NASA Administrator must take a formal step, certifying to Congress, before using funds for voluntary separation incentive payments. That reading fails because Congress is inside the federal government. Nothing in the section brings in any party outside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the NASA Administrator to certify information to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making the decision to use funds for separation incentives.
qwen_chat.s: unless the Administrator of NASA has first certified to Congress that such payments would not result in the loss of skills
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that certifying to Congress involves "participation" because it is a formal interaction. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to or notifications of Congress are inside the federal government and do not count as participation. Furthermore, the certification is a unilateral statement by the Administrator, not a consultation with an outside party.
